entries.summary: Tam-awan Village brings Cordillera huts, visual art and cultural activities together in Pinsao Proper, Baguio. Its landscaped hillside setting was designed to evoke a traditional village while making space for artists and visitors.
overview: Tam-awan Village is a cultural space adapted to Baguio’s hillside terrain. Its name means “vantage point,” and its development brought together art, landscape and traditional Cordillera architecture. The village preserves huts from Sagada and Kalinga, giving visitors a particular setting in which to learn about the region’s built culture. Art exhibitions and cultural activities are part of its purpose, alongside a café and a craft shop. The operator describes woven products, brass accessories and woodcarving among the crafts represented. These are features of a cultural venue in Baguio, rather than a claim that the site is itself a village in Sagada or Kalinga.
highlights: Look for the preserved Cordillera huts.
Explore the village’s art and craft focus.

entries.summary: Museo Kordilyera is the University of the Philippines Baguio’s ethnographic museum. Its collections and exhibitions focus on indigenous cultures of Northern Luzon, making it a distinct cultural visit on the university’s Governor Pack Road campus.
overview: Museo Kordilyera is UP Baguio’s ethnographic museum, dedicated to understanding and preserving indigenous cultures in Northern Luzon. Its collections, exhibitions and educational work provide ways to learn about the people of the Cordillera beyond a general introduction to Baguio. The museum publishes an online collection catalogue and resources about past exhibitions, including work concerning textiles and different Cordillera communities. Its shop also represents local handmade products. The institution is located on the UP Baguio campus on Governor Pack Road. Check the museum’s current exhibition information when planning a particular interest; material documented in an older virtual tour may describe a past installation.

entries.summary: Saint Louis University’s Museum of Igorot Cultures and Arts focuses on Cordillera cultural heritage. Located at the university on Bonifacio Street, it is a different institution from UP Baguio’s Museo Kordilyera.
overview: SLU’s Museum of Igorot Cultures and Arts presents material relating to Igorot cultural heritage, including traditional objects and art. It is located at Saint Louis University on Bonifacio Street in Baguio. The museum’s educational purpose connects collections with the preservation and appreciation of culture, rather than treating the objects simply as decorations. Its visitor guidance asks guests not to handle artifacts without permission. Group and guided visits need advance arrangements with the museum. Travelers planning a focused cultural visit should distinguish this university institution from Museo Kordilyera at UP Baguio and the independently named Baguio Museum.
highlights: Learn about traditional cultural objects and art.
Arrange a guided or group visit with the museum.
tips: Do not handle artifacts unless museum staff give permission.

entries.summary: Mines View Park is an overlook on Baguio’s northeastern edge, looking toward Itogon and former mining landscapes. Its observation deck is reached by a winding stone-covered stairway, making the viewpoint a specific outdoor stop.
overview: Mines View Park occupies a promontory on the northeastern outskirts of Baguio. The outlook takes in the mining town of Itogon, including former gold and copper mining areas, with a glimpse toward the Amburayan Valley. The observation deck lies below a winding, stone-covered stairway near the parking area. That layout is worth considering when deciding which part of the park to visit; the park’s Baguio location and the landscape seen from it are not the same administrative place.
